EVKX Model 3 Long Range MY2024–25 charging profile

parts.name: Body shell
parts.desc: The body provides the passenger compartment and attachment points for the vehicle’s systems. Its exterior surfaces also manage airflow, packaging and visibility.
parts.how: The floor-mounted battery and the body are different assemblies. The simplified model here is an explainer, not a structural repair drawing. Do not infer a structural-battery design or repair method from its shape.
facts: Body structure and battery casing are distinct references
Dimensions and equipment vary by build
Use repair documentation for actual construction

parts.name: Glass and glazing
parts.kicker: An open cabin, with layers of engineering.
parts.desc: Glazing brings light into the cabin while seals, coatings and laminated constructions influence noise and thermal comfort.
parts.how: Acoustic glazing and solar control address different physical effects. The appearance of a glass roof does not establish the specification of every pane or every trim.
facts: Equipment depends on the vehicle and market
Sunlight and cabin temperature are separate issues
The 3D glass is an illustrative material

parts.name: Lighting
parts.desc: Headlights and rear lamps combine road illumination with signals that communicate braking and manoeuvres to other road users.
parts.how: Beam behaviour depends on fitted hardware, software and local regulations. A visible lamp shape in this 2024 model does not prove a newer lighting feature is enabled.
facts: Check the controls and manual for your vehicle
Local rules affect available lighting functions
The gallery photograph identifies its model year

parts.name: Mirrors
parts.kicker: A useful view beyond the body.
parts.desc: Exterior mirrors help the driver monitor surrounding traffic and the area alongside the car. Cameras provide additional views with different limitations.
parts.how: A camera image, mirror and direct observation do not offer the same field of view. Adjust the mirrors for the driver and check visibility rather than assuming a displayed image removes blind spots.
facts: Adjustment is driver-specific
Keep mirrors and cameras clean
Illustrative geometry is not a visibility measurement

parts.name: Wheels and tyres
parts.kicker: The final connection to the road.
parts.desc: Tyres determine how steering, drive torque and braking forces reach the road. Wheel size and tyre specification can change efficiency and ride comfort.
parts.how: Pressure, load, temperature and tyre condition affect behaviour. Larger wheels do not automatically improve every aspect of grip or comfort. Choose approved sizes and maintain the specified pressures.
facts: Use the vehicle’s tyre-pressure label
Range figures can depend on wheel choice
The model is not a fitment or tyre-size guide

parts.name: Friction brakes
parts.desc: Disc brakes use friction to slow the wheels. Regenerative braking instead uses the drive system to recover some vehicle energy.
parts.how: Energy recovery can be limited by conditions such as battery temperature and state of charge. The driver must remain prepared to use the brake pedal; a familiar lift-off response is not guaranteed in every condition.
facts: Disc hardware in the model is illustrative
Regeneration and friction braking are different processes
Observe the vehicle’s warnings and service requirements

parts.name: Cabin and seating
parts.kicker: A space built around the drive.
parts.desc: Seat position, climate control, glazing and storage shape the everyday experience as much as a headline range figure.
parts.how: Inspect the actual vehicle for seat, trim and rear-screen equipment. This licensed 2024 interior model does not reproduce every Standard, Premium or Performance configuration.
facts: Try the driving position and rear-seat access
Check equipment on the ordered vehicle
Photographs retain their original model-year captions

parts.name: Touchscreens and controls
parts.desc: The touchscreen presents navigation, charging information and many vehicle settings. Other functions use steering-wheel or dedicated physical controls.
parts.how: Menus and hardware can change with software and production updates. Check the vehicle itself rather than using this 2024 render as a menu or screen-size reference.
facts: The model illustrates an earlier cabin
Current trim specifications are a separate reference
Use your vehicle’s manual for operating instructions

parts.name: High-voltage battery
parts.kicker: Energy stored low in the car.
parts.desc: The traction battery stores energy for propulsion and other high-voltage loads. Its management system monitors operation while thermal management helps maintain suitable conditions.
parts.how: Nominal capacity, usable energy, cell chemistry and supplier are different attributes. A published number for one pack is not a universal Model 3 specification; this explorer does not assign one battery capacity to the whole range.
facts: Battery capacity is not inferred from advertised range
State of charge is different from charging power
The pack shape and internal layout are illustrative

parts.name: Rear drive unit
parts.desc: The rear drive unit combines an electric motor with reduction gearing to drive the rear wheels. Power electronics control the electrical supply.
parts.how: Torque at the motor and torque at the wheel are different quantities. Acceleration also depends on tyres, vehicle mass, traction, available battery power and conditions.
facts: RWD and AWD references are kept separate
No motor output is inferred from the 3D shape
The internal geometry is educational

parts.name: Front drive unit
parts.kicker: An additional driven axle on AWD cars.
parts.desc: Dual-motor versions use a front drive unit as well as a rear unit. A rear-wheel-drive vehicle does not acquire a front motor because it appears in this generic exploded model.
parts.how: The vehicle manages torque between driven axles according to operating conditions. This model shows an illustrative AWD architecture rather than identifying the hardware of a specific vehicle.
facts: Shown for the AWD architecture
Not fitted to a RWD configuration merely because it is visible here
Exact hardware requires vehicle-specific documentation

parts.name: Power electronics
parts.kicker: Control the motor, not just the current.
parts.desc: An inverter controls the electrical power delivered to an electric motor. The traction battery supplies DC while the motor drive requires controlled electrical waveforms.
parts.how: During energy recovery, the system also manages electrical energy returning from the drive units. Physical arrangement and component specification depend on the installed drive system.
facts: This is a functional illustration
DC and controlled motor power are different stages
High-voltage components are not owner-serviceable

parts.name: Heat pump and thermal system
parts.kicker: Move heat where it is useful.
parts.desc: A heat pump transfers heat between parts of the thermal system. Vehicle thermal management also manages the needs of the cabin, battery and powertrain.
parts.how: Moving heat can reduce the electrical energy required for cabin warming compared with creating all that heat resistively. Actual efficiency depends on conditions, temperature and operating mode.
facts: A diagram is not a refrigerant routing plan
Battery preparation can use energy before a stop
No fixed winter efficiency benefit is promised

parts.name: Low-voltage system
parts.desc: A separate low-voltage system powers control electronics and other vehicle functions. It works alongside the high-voltage traction system.
parts.how: Low-voltage battery type and service procedures can differ across vehicles. Use the instructions for the installed system instead of assuming every Model 3 has the same nominal voltage or chemistry.
facts: Low voltage does not mean every task is safe to perform
Follow the vehicle-specific service instructions
No universal replacement specification is stated here

parts.name: Front suspension
parts.desc: The front suspension supports the car and controls wheel motion while the steering system sets wheel direction. Springs, dampers and links have different jobs.
parts.how: Springs support load and store energy; dampers control motion. Geometry, alignment, tyres and settings affect how the complete system responds. The simplified components are not dimensional engineering data.
facts: Alignment is a service setting, not a styling feature
Wheel travel is not shown to scale
Performance equipment varies by trim

parts.name: Rear suspension
parts.desc: The rear suspension supports the body while allowing the wheels to move with the road. Links locate the wheels and dampers manage their motion.
parts.how: Changes in load or tyre specification can affect the way a car rides and responds. A visually similar assembly is not proof of identical damping, geometry or parts across trims.
facts: The assembly is illustrative
Do not infer interchangeable parts
Use the correct service and alignment information

parts.name: Charging inlet
parts.desc: The inlet connects the vehicle to compatible charging equipment. AC charging and DC fast charging feed the vehicle through different electrical paths.
parts.how: For AC, an onboard charger converts supplied AC into DC. A compatible DC fast charger supplies DC through the vehicle’s managed charging system. Plug shape, adapters and capabilities depend on the market and vehicle.
facts: AC input is not the same as DC peak power
The gallery shows an older European inlet
Check cable and adapter compatibility for your car

parts.name: Cameras
parts.kicker: Inputs, not a promise of autonomy.
parts.desc: Cameras provide views used by vehicle features and driver-assistance systems. Dirt, obstruction, weather and visibility can affect the information available.
parts.how: A camera shown in the model does not establish software entitlement or regulatory availability. The consumer supervised system still requires an attentive driver; use the FSD tracker for country evidence.
facts: Keep the relevant camera areas unobstructed
Feature availability is vehicle- and market-specific
No autonomous capability is inferred from this model

parts.name: Cabin climate system
parts.kicker: Comfort is an energy system too.
parts.desc: Fans, ducts, filters and thermal equipment move and condition air for the cabin. Demisting and passenger comfort place different demands on the system.
parts.how: Preconditioning while connected to power can prepare the vehicle before a journey. The energy used by climate control is part of overall vehicle consumption, not a separate free resource.
facts: Set conditions for passengers and visibility
Filters and airflow need maintenance
No fixed climate-energy penalty is assumed
